outcome: Since 26 January 2024 no refereed resolution, restricted-case verification or bound improvement on this problem appears in these sources: the one live claim is André Unterberger's arXiv preprint (2001.10956) whose Section 9 asserts the conjecture for Γ0(M) (first posted 15 January 2024, eleven days before the freeze, and revised through 12 February 2026) with no expert engagement found, and the in-window items are a 2024 upper bound on the number of violating Hecke-Maass forms on Γ0(N) (Choi, Lee, Lee and Lim) and a 2024 large-sieve paper (Pascadi, published 2026) that does not move the eigenvalue bound.
problem_asks: The statement asks for three things. (1) Scope: the eigenvalue assertion is made for 'congruence subgroups' with no further restriction, so it covers the principal congruence subgroups Γ(N), the Hecke-type groups Γ0(N) and Γ1(N), and congruence subgroups with a nontrivial character; the frozen wording does not name SL2(Z) as the ambient group, and the standard reading takes congruence subgroups of SL2(Z). (2) Object: for each such Γ, the Maass wave forms (non-zero square-integrable eigenfunctions of the hyperbolic Laplacian Δ on Γ\H of cuspidal type) have Laplace eigenvalue λ ≥ 1/4. (3) Equivalent form, per Wikipedia: the cuspidal spectrum of each such Γ avoids the open interval (0, 1/4); the endpoint 1/4 is permitted. Part (1) and part (2) are separate: the statement could hold for some congruence subgroups and fail for others, and a result on one family does not answer the other.

events.what_happened: André Unterberger (Université de Reims, sole author), arXiv:2001.10956, 'The Ramanujan-Petersson and Selberg conjectures for Maass forms'. The Selberg claim first appears in v9 (15 Jan 2024): the abstract ends 'The Selberg conjecture for Hecke's group Γ0(M) follows as well', the title gains 'and Selberg', and the comments field reads 'I have included, as a last section, a proof of Selberg's conjecture, and completed the title accordingly'. The same abstract and comment are carried by v10 (6 May 2024) and by v13 (21 Oct 2025) and v16 (12 Feb 2026). v8 (16 Feb 2022) and v1 (29 Jan 2020) do not mention Selberg. Section 9 ('The Selberg conjecture') states Theorem 9.2: 'Given M, there is no cusp-form N for the group Γ = Γ0(M) such that ΔN = (1−ν²)/4 N with Re(ν²) > 0', and concludes 'Hence, ν1 is pure imaginary, and the eigenvalue 1−ν1²/4 is at least 1/4'. The proof 'follows the same lines as that of our attempt of the Ramanujan case', with Proposition 9.1 replacing Theorem 8.2 of that argument and the spectral decomposition imported from Deshouillers–Iwaniec. No journal reference is listed on arXiv.
events.revisions: v1 29 Jan 2020 (title 'The Ramanujan-Petersson conjecture for Maass forms', Ramanujan only); v2 26 May 2020 withdrawn; v3 9 Jun 2020; v4 26 Jan 2021; v5 23 Aug 2021 withdrawn; v6 17 Sep 2021; v7 9 Jan 2022; v8 16 Feb 2022 (Ramanujan only); v9 15 Jan 2024 (first Selberg section and 'Selberg' added to title); v10 6 May 2024 (abstract and comment unchanged in the fetched text); v11 26 Feb 2025; v12 12 Mar 2025; v13 21 Oct 2025; v14 7 Nov 2025; v15 17 Nov 2025; v16 12 Feb 2026 (comment: '(pseudodifferential) Section 7 has been rewritten, so as to make easier reading'). v11, v12, v14, v15 were not opened individually; their dates come from the v16 version list.
events.delivers: If Section 9 is correct, no Maass cusp eigenvalue in (0, 1/4) exists for Γ0(M) for any M, which is the conjectured direction for that family. The claim is stated only for Γ0(M), and the text read does not say whether the character is trivial. It says nothing about Γ(N), Γ1(N), or congruence subgroups with characters.
events.remains: The assertion for every other congruence subgroup of the kind listed in problem_asks: principal Γ(N), Γ1(N), congruence subgroups with a nontrivial character, and general congruence subgroups not of the form Γ0(M). The Ramanujan-Petersson claim in the same preprint is a different problem (see unterberger-2020-ramanujan-claim).
events.time_since_posted: 33 months since v9 (15 Jan 2024) to 13 Oct 2026; the latest version v16 (12 Feb 2026) is 8 months old. No journal reference, no zbMATH or MathSciNet entry, no review, no expert commentary and no citing paper was found in the searches listed under search. The Wikipedia Ramanujan–Petersson article (last edited 12 Aug 2026) still says the Maass case is open 'as of 2025' and does not mention this preprint; the Wikipedia Selberg article (last edited 19 June 2025) does not mention it either.
events.doubts: (a) Single-author preprint with no journal reference; no referee, reviewer or expert is named anywhere in the arXiv record, and the searches found no public engagement. (b) The Selberg section is not an independent argument: it follows 'the same lines' as the author's Ramanujan argument and replaces only one proposition of it, so its validity rests on Sections 7 to 9 as a whole, which the Ramanujan claim itself has not had reviewed. (c) Scope changed between versions: the Selberg claim was added in v9 (Jan 2024), four years after the Ramanujan claim was first posted, with a title change; the v2 and v5 withdrawals predate it. (d) The same author's companion (arXiv:2004.00284) describes an earlier version as 'incorrect at some point' and its current version 'follows closely the proof of the Ramanujan-Petersson conjecture for Maass forms arXiv:2001.10956'. (e) I found no specific error identified in a key step of this argument and no withdrawal of the Selberg section.

withdrawn.what: The whole arXiv entry has versions v2 (26 May 2020) and v5 (23 Aug 2021) marked withdrawn. Neither withdrawn version contains the Selberg section (both predate v9). The reason and the withdrawing party are not stated.

events.direction: If correct, it cuts toward the conjecture for Γ0(M): it asserts that the cuspidal spectrum on Γ0(M) has no point in (0, 1/4). It exhibits no counterexample and is not a claim that the conjecture fails anywhere.
people: André Unterberger (Université de Reims; sole author)

events.what_happened: The same arXiv preprint, 2001.10956, first posted 29 Jan 2020 under the title 'The Ramanujan-Petersson conjecture for Maass forms'. Its abstract claims a proof of the Ramanujan-Petersson conjecture for Maass forms of SL(2,Z) 'with the help of automorphic distribution theory and pseudodifferential analysis', presented as an alternative in which 'the plane takes the place usually ascribed to the hyperbolic half-plane'. This is a separate problem from the one assigned here and is recorded as a discounted event because it shares the preprint and the Selberg section depends on it.
events.revisions: See unterberger-2024-selberg-section for the full version list (v1 to v16).
events.delivers: Claimed proof of the Ramanujan-Petersson conjecture for Maass forms of SL(2,Z). Not a statement about the 1/4 eigenvalue bound.
events.remains: The whole of this problem: the claimed Ramanujan result says nothing directly about λ1 ≥ 1/4.
events.time_since_posted: About 6 years 8 months to 13 Oct 2026; no engagement found (see unterberger-2024-selberg-section).
events.doubts: Same as unterberger-2024-selberg-section: single author, no referee named, no public engagement found; the Selberg section depends on this argument.
events.direction: Claims the Ramanujan-Petersson bound for SL(2,Z) Maass forms, which is a different conjecture; it does not say which way the 1/4 eigenvalue question goes.

events.what_happened: Companion preprint by the same author, arXiv:2004.00284, 'A unified scheme of approach to the Ramanujan conjecture', first posted 1 Apr 2020. Its comments field in v12 (22 Mar 2026) reads 'This is a complete revision of the former (incorrect at some point) version', 'The present version follows closely the proof of the Ramanujan-Petersson conjecture for Maass forms arXiv:2001.10956', and 'There are however interesting differences'. The body was not read; a search snippet describes it as covering the holomorphic case, which I did not verify.
events.revisions: v1 1 Apr 2020; v2 26 May 2020 (withdrawn); v3 30 Jun 2020; v4 6 Oct 2021; v5 19 Jan 2022; v6 27 Feb 2023; v7 1 Mar 2023; v8 15 May 2024; v9 23 Jun 2025 (withdrawn); v10 1 Jul 2025; v11 27 Nov 2025 (withdrawn); v12 22 Mar 2026.
events.delivers: Not a statement about Maass forms' 1/4 eigenvalue bound, as far as the metadata and comments read show. Its content is an analogue of the author's Ramanujan argument.
events.time_since_posted: About 6 years 6 months; no engagement found.
events.doubts: The comments field itself says an earlier version was 'incorrect at some point'. Versions v2, v9 and v11 are withdrawn. The current version is a close follow of the unverified Ramanujan argument, so it is not an independent check of it.

withdrawn.what: Versions v2 (26 May 2020), v9 (23 Jun 2025) and v11 (27 Nov 2025) are marked withdrawn. The reasons are not stated.

events.direction: Not applicable to the 1/4 bound; discounted as an analogue (Ramanujan-type statement).

events.what_happened: Dohoon Choi, Min Lee, Youngmin Lee and Subong Lim, arXiv:2402.11761, 'The number of automorphic representations of GL2 with exceptional eigenvalues', v1 only. Using the Arthur–Selberg trace formula they bound the total dimension of K0(J)-fixed vectors of non-tempered cuspidal representations of GL2 over a number field F. The introduction's Corollary 1.2(1) gives, for F = Q, an upper bound on the number of weight-0 Hecke–Maass cusp forms on Γ0(N) that do not satisfy Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture: 𝒩(Γ0(N)) ≪ [SL2(Z):Γ0(N)]/(log N)², as N → ∞. The paper cites the Kim–Sarnak bound λ ≥ 1/4 − (7/64)² as the best known and claims no new lower bound and no existence result.
events.delivers: An upper bound on the number of Hecke–Maass cusp forms of weight 0 on Γ0(N) with eigenvalue below 1/4, of order index over (log N)². This is a bound on the count of exceptions, not on their existence: it does not show there are none, and it does not change the lower bound for λ1. It covers Γ0(N) only.
events.remains: Whether any exceptional form exists on any congruence subgroup; the conjecture for Γ(N), Γ1(N), congruence subgroups with characters and the other families in problem_asks. The bound is an upper bound that may be zero.
events.time_since_posted: About 32 months; no review, citation or commentary found in the searches listed under search.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture: it constrains how many violating forms there can be, and asserts nothing about λ1 bounds. Whether the count of exceptions is a quantity the statement names is for the judging pass (see competing_reading).

events.what_happened: Alexandru Pascadi (University of Oxford), arXiv:2404.04239, first posted 5 Apr 2024 as 'Large sieve inequalities for exceptional Maass forms and applications'; the current title is 'Large sieve inequalities for exceptional Maass forms and the greatest prime factor of n²+1'. The paper proves large-sieve inequalities for Fourier coefficients of exceptional Maass forms of fixed level, weighted by sequences with sparse Fourier transforms. The abstract says these 'give the first savings in the exceptional spectrum for the critical case of sequences as long as the level'. Applications: the greatest prime factor of n²+1 exceeds n^1.3 infinitely often; equidistribution in progressions to moduli up to x^(5/8−o(1)). Published as Forum of Mathematics, Pi 14 (2026), e8 (received 9 Jan 2025, accepted 5 Oct 2025, per the journal listing in the search results).
events.revisions: v1 5 Apr 2024 (125 KB; the first version's abstract, per a search snippet, said the applications 'completely eliminate the dependency on Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture' in earlier results of Lichtman and the author); v2 8 Jan 2025 ('small improvements and removed two applications (to appear in a separate preprint)'); v3 15 Jan 2026 ('incorporates referees' comments'; journal reference Forum Math. Pi 14 (2026) e8).
events.delivers: Savings in large-sieve sums over exceptional Maass forms of fixed level, and consequent improvements in the applications listed. It does not change the lower bound on λ1 for any congruence subgroup and does not change the exceptional-spectrum parameter bound: the abstract's 'first savings' concern sums of Fourier coefficients, not the eigenvalue itself. The v1 claim that earlier results no longer depend on the conjecture is a conditional-to-unconditional statement about other theorems, not a result on this problem.
events.remains: The whole of this problem: the lower bound λ1 ≥ 1/4 on every congruence subgroup.

checked_by.who: Referees of Forum of Mathematics, Pi (names not given in the source)
checked_by.what_they_did: Refereed; the v3 comment says the revision 'incorporates referees' comments'. Acceptance 5 Oct 2025 per the journal listing (search result only).

events.doubts: Scope shrank between versions: v1's claim to remove dependence on Selberg's conjecture in earlier results was reduced when v2 removed two applications 'to appear in a separate preprint'. This is a scope change, not a doubt about the sieve results. The current abstract says the paper 'announces applications'; I did not check whether the dependence claim survives in the separate preprint, which I could not locate.
events.direction: Not a statement about λ1: it gives savings in sums over exceptional forms. If read as bearing on the problem, it removes conditionality from other theorems but leaves the conjecture itself unchanged.

events.what_happened: Liyang Yang, 'On Exceptional Maass Forms', arXiv:2011.09054, posted 18 Nov 2020 and withdrawn 30 Nov 2020 (v2). The abstract (as fetched in part) claims that the Ramanujan-Petersson conjecture at a fixed prime not dividing the level, for non-exceptional Maass forms, implies that conjecture for all Maass forms of that level 'and Selberg's 1/4-eigenvalue conjecture simultaneously', and claims an improvement of the Kim–Sarnak 7/64 bound on Satake parameters for exceptional forms. The comments field reads 'There are typos in Lemma 8-10. Proof of Theorem B is incomplete'.
events.revisions: v1 18 Nov 2020 (18 KB); v2 30 Nov 2020 (1 KB, withdrawn by the author).
events.delivers: A conditional reduction only: it would give the 1/4 bound for level-N Maass forms if the Ramanujan-Petersson conjecture held at one fixed prime for non-exceptional forms. Not unconditional.
events.remains: The unconditional statement for every congruence subgroup; Theorem B, the step the paper claims, is by its own comment incomplete.
events.doubts: The author's own comment: 'Proof of Theorem B is incomplete', with typos in Lemmas 8–10; the paper was then withdrawn.

withdrawn.what: Whole paper withdrawn by the author (v2). The comments field retains the incompleteness note.

events.direction: A conditional implication in the conjectured direction; it asserts no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Andrew R. Booker, Min Lee and Andreas Strömbergsson, 'Twist-minimal trace formulas and the Selberg eigenvalue conjecture', arXiv:1803.06016, first posted 15 Mar 2018 (v2 17 Apr 2020), 'to appear in JLMS' (Journal of the London Mathematical Society; DOI 10.1112/jlms.12349). Theorem 1.1, as quoted from the paper: 'The Selberg eigenvalue conjecture is true for Γ1(N) for N≤880, and for Γ(N) for N≤226.' The paper also quotes Huxley for level N≤18 (Remarks 1.3). The conditional result, Theorem 1.2, assumes Artin's conjecture and concerns classification of Artin representations of small conductor.
events.revisions: v1 15 Mar 2018 (56 KB); v2 17 Apr 2020 (57 KB, current; comment '64 pages, to appear in JLMS'). Journal publication 2020 per the Wiley listing in the search results.
events.delivers: An unconditional verification of the conjecture (no eigenvalues in (0, 1/4)) for Γ1(N) at levels N≤880 and for Γ(N) at levels N≤226. Restricted to those levels; this is a case-by-case settlement of the statement for finitely many levels, which the statement does not ask for in these terms.
events.remains: Γ1(N) for N>880, Γ(N) for N>226, and every other congruence subgroup (including those with characters) at any level.

checked_by.who: Referees of the Journal of the London Mathematical Society (names not in the source)
checked_by.what_they_did: Refereed and published in JLMS (2020); acceptance per the Wiley listing in search results, which I did not open.

events.directly_checkable: The verification is a computer-assisted trace-formula computation. The paper says its numerical results are rigorous apart from possible bugs in the software and hardware (ar5iv Remarks). It is not a proof-assistant check.
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture for the listed levels: no counterexample at those levels.

events.what_happened: Andrew R. Booker and Andreas Strömbergsson, 'Numerical computations with the trace formula and the Selberg eigenvalue conjecture', J. reine angew. Math. 607 (2007), 113–161, DOI 10.1515/CRELLE.2007.047. The abstract (Bristol portal) states: 'We verify the Selberg eigenvalue conjecture for congruence groups of small squarefree conductor.' The method is the Selberg trace formula, which can handle cases where the eigenvalue 1/4 occurs, and the paper improves on Huxley's result.
events.revisions: Published 2007 (June). An earlier preprint date was not established.
events.delivers: The conjecture verified for congruence groups of small squarefree conductor. The Bristol page gives no numerical bound on the conductor. A search snippet reported q ≤ 857, which I did not verify.
events.remains: Non-squarefree conductors; all conductors above the (unquantified) bound.

checked_by.who: Referees of Crelle's Journal (names not in the source)

events.directly_checkable: Computer-assisted trace-formula computation. A companion programs page is reported in search results at www2.math.uu.se/~ast10761/stfz; it could not be opened (certificate error).
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture for the listed congruence groups.

events.what_happened: Henry H. Kim and Peter Sarnak, appendix to H. Kim, 'Functoriality for the exterior square of GL4 and the symmetric fourth of GL2', J. Amer. Math. Soc. 16 (2003), 139–183. The bound λ1 ≥ 975/4096 (= 1/4 − (7/64)²) for congruence subgroups is attributed to this appendix in the sources read: Wikipedia ('best bound currently known is 975/4096 ≈ 0.238, due to Kim & Sarnak (2003)'), and Choi et al. (opened), which cites 'the Kim–Sarnak bound λf ≥ 1/4 − (7/64)²'. The JAMS page returned 403 and the appendix text was not read.
events.revisions: Journal publication 2003 (vol. 16); no arXiv version found.
events.delivers: Lowers the lower bound on the first eigenvalue of congruence subgroups to 975/4096 ≈ 0.238 (from Kim–Shahidi's 66/289 in 2002 and Selberg's 3/16). Quantitative, not a settlement.
events.remains: The whole gap [975/4096, 1/4) for every congruence subgroup, and the conjecture itself.

checked_by.who: Journal of the American Mathematical Society (refereed; referees not named)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published in JAMS 16 (2003); the appendix's content was not read directly.

events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture as a bound: no eigenvalue in (0, 975/4096) for congruence subgroups.

events.what_happened: Kim and Shahidi (2002), as cited in a bibliography snippet from a search result: λ1 ≥ 66/289 for congruence subgroups. Superseded by Kim–Sarnak (2003). Recorded for the bound history; not opened.
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture as a bound; superseded.

events.what_happened: Huxley (1985): the conjecture verified for groups of level N≤18, as stated in Booker–Lee–Strömbergsson's Remarks 1.3 ('who proved the Selberg eigenvalue conjecture for groups of level N≤18'). Booker and Strömbergsson cite Huxley's 'Introduction to Kloostermania' (Banach Center Publ. 17, 1985, pp. 217–306). A Duke Math. J. 1985 paper by Huxley, 'On the spectrum of the Hecke groups', is also in search results; its page returned no abstract, so it is not established which Huxley publication holds the N≤18 claim.
events.delivers: Verification for groups of level N≤18, as stated secondhand; the groups are not specified in the source I read.
events.remains: Levels N≥19 and the rest of the problem.
events.doubts: The N≤18 claim rests on one secondary citation (Booker–Lee–Strömbergsson). The primary Huxley publications were not readable (Duke page empty; Banach Center reference not opened).
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture for the listed levels.
people: Huxley (initials and affiliation not established from the sources read)

events.what_happened: Atle Selberg (1965) stated the conjecture that the cuspidal Laplace eigenvalues on congruence subgroups are at least 1/4, and proved λ1 ≥ 3/16 for the principal congruence subgroups. Per Wikipedia, citing Selberg (1965, p. 13) in 'Theory of Numbers'. The primary was not opened.
events.delivers: Lower bound 3/16 for λ1 of the principal congruence subgroups (per Wikipedia). The conjecture itself is stated, not established.
events.remains: The conjecture in full; the 1/4 bound.
events.direction: Establishes the weaker bound and states the conjectured bound.

events.what_happened: Morten S. Risager, 'On Selberg's small eigenvalue conjecture and residual eigenvalues', arXiv:0707.2332, first posted 16 Jul 2007. Theorem 1.1: Selberg's conjecture (Conjecture 1.1) holds if and only if a conjecture about the non-existence of residual eigenvalues for a perturbed family of operators in (0, 1/4) holds (Conjecture 1.2). A search snippet gives the journal as J. reine angew. Math. 656 (2011), 179–211; not verified in the fetched page, which lists none.
events.revisions: v1 16 Jul 2007 (from the arXiv abstract page). Later versions were not checked.
events.delivers: Equivalence only: the conjecture is equivalent to the residual-eigenvalue statement. No settlement of either. The search snippet says the equivalence is stated for Hecke congruence groups Γ0(q) with characters induced from a Dirichlet character.
events.remains: The conjecture in full, and the residual-eigenvalue statement.

checked_by.who: Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik (Crelle), per a search snippet
checked_by.what_they_did: Published (2011), per search snippet only; not verified.

events.direction: Neutral: a reformulation, not a test of the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Sugata Mondal, 'On largeness and multiplicity of the first eigenvalue of hyperbolic surfaces', arXiv:1406.1080, first posted 4 Jun 2014 (v2 8 Oct 2014); Math. Z. 281 (2015), 333–348. For closed hyperbolic surfaces of genus two, the set of surfaces with first eigenvalue λ1 > 1/4 is unbounded and separates the moduli space. This concerns closed surfaces, not congruence subgroups.
events.revisions: v1 4 Jun 2014 ('at least 1/4'); v2 8 Oct 2014 ('greater than 1/4', unbounded); Math. Z. 2015.
events.delivers: Existence of closed genus-two hyperbolic surfaces with λ1 > 1/4. A different question (closed surfaces, not congruence subgroups); discounted for this problem.

checked_by.who: Referees of Mathematische Zeitschrift (names not in the source)

events.direction: Different question: it shows large first eigenvalues occur on some closed surfaces. It does not touch congruence subgroups.

events.what_happened: Emilio A. Lauret, 'A numerical study on exceptional eigenvalues of certain congruence subgroups of SO(n,1) and SU(n,1)', arXiv:1212.0674, submitted 4 Dec 2012 (v2 16 Dec 2012). Numerical experiments 'suggest exceptional eigenvalues for some arithmetic subgroups of SU(3,1), SU(4,1), and SU(5,1)' and a lower bound better than the known bound for some SO(4,1), SO(6,1), SO(8,1) and SU(2,1) subgroups. The paper says the exceptional eigenvalues 'contradicts the generalized Selberg (and Ramanujan) conjecture in these cases' (sic). The results are numerical, not proofs.
events.delivers: Numerical evidence for exceptional eigenvalues in unitary and orthogonal groups of real rank one, not SL2. It does not concern SL2(Z) or its congruence subgroups, and it is not a proof.
events.remains: The statement for SL2 congruence subgroups, which this paper does not address.
events.doubts: Numerical evidence only; the paper's own results are heuristic-numeric and not claimed rigorous.
events.direction: Cuts against a generalised (unitary-group) version of the conjecture, in cases the paper names. Discounted for the bullet, which is stated for congruence subgroups of Maass wave forms, but a reader could read the unrestricted wording as covering these families.
events.object: Numerically computed exceptional (sub-1/4) Laplace eigenvalues on some arithmetic subgroups of SU(3,1), SU(4,1) and SU(5,1). The paper gives no explicit exhibited form; its evidence is numerical lattice-point error terms.

events.what_happened: Laura Monk, 'Typical hyperbolic surfaces have an optimal spectral gap', arXiv:2601.15157, submitted 21 Jan 2026, a survey for Current Developments in Mathematics 2025. The abstract (joint work with Nalini Anantharaman, per its text) states that 'the spectral gap is asymptotically bounded above by 1/4' for large hyperbolic surfaces and that, for Weil–Petersson random genus-g surfaces, the spectral gap exceeds 1/4 − ε with probability tending to one.
events.revisions: v1 only, per the fetched abstract page.
events.delivers: A random-surface analogue: typical large (non-congruence) surfaces have λ1 near 1/4. Not a statement about congruence subgroups.
events.direction: Neither for nor against: a random-surface analogue of the 1/4 barrier, discounted.

disputes.summary: Unterberger's arXiv preprint (v9 onward) claims a proof of the conjecture for Γ0(M), but Wikipedia's Ramanujan–Petersson article (edited 12 Aug 2026) still calls the Maass case open 'as of 2025' and the Selberg article (edited 19 June 2025) gives 975/4096 as the best bound. The preprint has no referee, journal reference or public response. Yang's 2020 paper (withdrawn; Theorem B incomplete) addresses the same question conditionally.

summary: Nothing in these sources settles or improves this problem in the window. Wikipedia's Selberg article (last edited 19 June 2025) lists the conjecture as open with Kim–Sarnak's 975/4096 as the best bound, and the Ramanujan–Petersson article (last edited 12 Aug 2026) still treats the Maass case as open 'as of 2025'. The only live claim is Unterberger's arXiv:2001.10956, which has two dates on its Selberg section: the section first appears in v9 (15 Jan 2024), eleven days before the freeze, so under the §5.1 rule I have dated the event to that version; the in-window items are its revisions v10 to v16 (last 12 Feb 2026), not new arguments. Its Section 9 asserts that no cuspidal eigenvalue in (0, 1/4) exists for Γ0(M), which is a restricted case; principal Γ(N), Γ1(N) and congruence subgroups with characters are not addressed in the text read. The argument is said to 'follow the same lines' as the author's Ramanujan argument, which rests on the same unreviewed machinery. I found no journal reference, zbMATH or MathSciNet entry, review, expert commentary, citing paper, or identified error in a key step, and no withdrawal of the Selberg section; the same author's companion (arXiv:2004.00284) calls an earlier version 'incorrect at some point' and withdrew three versions. The two in-window papers do not settle anything: Choi, Lee, Lee and Lim (Feb 2024) bound the number of violating Hecke–Maass forms on Γ0(N) by an index over (log N)², which constrains the count but does not show there are none or move the λ1 bound; Pascadi (Apr 2024, Forum Math. Pi 2026) gives large-sieve savings in exceptional-spectrum sums and leaves λ1 and the Kim–Sarnak parameter unchanged in the sources read. The historical record is: Selberg (1965) 3/16 and the conjecture; Kim–Shahidi (2002) 66/289 from a search snippet only; Huxley (1985) level N≤18, per a secondary citation only; Booker–Strömbergsson (2007, Crelle) small squarefree conductor; Booker–Lee–Strömbergsson (2018/2020, JLMS) Γ1(N) for N≤880 and Γ(N) for N≤226, unconditional; Risager (2007) the equivalence to a residual-eigenvalue statement; Kim–Sarnak (2003) λ1 ≥ 975/4096. Discounted events: Mondal (2014) on closed genus-two surfaces; Lauret (2012) numerical exceptional eigenvalues for SU(n,1) and SO(n,1) subgroups; Monk (2026) on random surfaces; Yang (2020) conditional and withdrawn; and Unterberger's Ramanujan claim, which is a different problem. AI: no AI system is named in any source for this problem. Unterberger's full text was scanned in two chunks for AI and software mentions and none appears beyond a LaTeXML footer. The 2024 Choi et al. and Pascadi papers were read through their acknowledgements with no AI mention. The OpenAI 'openai/math' repository (719 manuscripts, reported published 6 Oct 2026 in secondary coverage) has a README that names no model, and its CONTENTS.md, read in six chunks through a summarising fetch rather than verbatim, lists no entry on Maass forms, Selberg, Laplacian eigenvalues or congruence subgroups. AIM's 'AI and number theory' workshop (27–30 May 2026) problem list was checked only through its .lean benchmark file, which has no item on this problem; the PDF did not parse. Searches for AlphaProof, AlphaEvolve, Gemini Deep Think, Claude, GPT, OpenAI and language-model claims on this conjecture returned nothing relevant. Close calls: (1) the date of Unterberger's Selberg section (15 Jan 2024, pre-window) against its in-window revisions; (2) whether Choi et al.'s bound on violating forms moves a quantity the statement names, or constrains a count that may be zero; I record it as a count-bound and not a settlement; (3) whether Pascadi's paper bears on the problem at all, which I record as adjacent because its savings are in large-sieve sums and not in λ1.
competing_reading: Read 'congruence subgroups' as the statement does, with no restriction, and the Unterberger claim settles only the family Γ0(M), while Choi et al. bounds only a count; then nothing in the window moves the problem, and it stays open. The opposite reading takes Unterberger's Section 9 at face value, counts it as a restricted-case resolution of the conjecture for Γ0(M), and reads Choi et al.'s bound on the number of violators as moving the exceptional count that the conjecture asserts is zero; on that reading there is a pending resolution for one family, but its first public argument predates the window by eleven days. A third reading treats Lauret's numerical SU(n,1) exceptional eigenvalues as counterexamples to a generalised congruence version, which would make the unrestricted wording false for those families even though the bullet is stated for SL2-type Maass forms.
what_would_settle_it: (1) A journal acceptance, referee report or published expert verification of Sections 7 to 9 of arXiv:2001.10956, or an identified error in them; (2) an explicit statement of Theorem 9.2's character and congruence scope, and whether the argument covers Γ(N) and other congruence subgroups; (3) a resolution for the remaining congruence subgroups, or an explicit exceptional form on a congruence subgroup of SL2(Z), or a rigorous statement that none exists; (4) reading the Kim–Sarnak appendix (JAMS 16, 2003), Huxley's 1985 paper, and Booker–Strömbergsson 2007 directly to fix the exact scope of the bounds and verifications; (5) a verbatim scan of the OpenAI CONTENTS.md and of the full AIM problem-list PDF for any entry on this problem.
